Sasha —

Thanks for the checklist and the timeline. High level answer up front: our recommended execution for HelixWorks is to adopt Module 4 (Processor-to-Processor) as the primary path for telemetry exports, combined with a narrow Module 2 (Controller-to-Processor) clause set for administrative/contractual handoffs where the controller relationship is explicit. Reasoning in short:

- Operational alignment: Most of the telemetry we process for HelixWorks is batched telemetry ingest where Redwood acts as a processor that performs enrichment and routing. Module 4 maps to that operational model and avoids mis-characterization at the access/control layer.
- Fallback/resilience: For customer configurations where HelixWorks retains control over user identity mappings and issues direct instructions to Redwood, Module 2 clauses are retained as a narrowly scoped fallback.
- Controls: We will bind the routing fallback to a policy flag in the console (route_override) and a documented runbook for incident-triggered transfers.

Immediate next steps I can own:
1) Share our SCCs addendum template populated for HelixWorks and a redacted evidence matrix (SOC 2 pointer, DPIA excerpt, subprocessors list).
2) Loop in Legal (Neha) to confirm Module 4/2 combination and any clause tailoring.
3) Provide a DocuSign addendum link and target a signature within 10 business days.

Attaching: RDW_SCCs_Addendum_template.docx (for review).

If that approach looks OK to you, we'll escalate to Neha for the legal sign-off and return a single consolidated packet.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Head of Customer Security
Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: SCCs - module guidance & evidence request for UK transfer

Marcus / Kim —

Quick legal read: Module 4 as primary with a tightly-scoped Module 2 fallback is defensible provided we meet three conditions:

1) Data flow mapping: We must produce a concise flow diagram that shows Redwood never assumes controller-level decision-making for HelixWorks telemetry except in the narrow administrative cases. That diagram needs to be included in the evidence packet (DPIA excerpt + flow).
2) Subprocessor commitments: Ensure all subprocessors invoked for telemetry processing have contractual parity and can be stepped out of the processing chain on request; add the subprocessors CSV to the pack.
3) Technical controls: Strong cryptographic separation (customer-specific keying or tenant isolation) and KV-cache purging on contract termination must be documented.

I'll make two edits to the addendum template for module mapping and add a short clause requiring a routing policy (console flag + audit entry) before fallback is invoked. Also recommend we include the following docs in the packet for HelixWorks:
- redwood-soc2-report-2025.pdf (SOC 2 summary page + scope)
- DPIA_telemetry_excerpt.pdf (redacted)
- subprocessors_export.csv
- evidence_matrix_redwood.csv (control references to SOC2/ISO/SCCs)

I'll draft the DocuSign wrapper and share it to Marcus to send to HelixWorks once the flow diagram is attached.

Neha
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
